mission: Use GitHub, O*NET, and Codecademy as complementary benchmark lenses for Buddy's coding, professional-task, and real-world work capabilities.

source_roles.github: software-development workflow, repository operations, collaboration, CI/CD, version control, project delivery
source_roles.onet: occupation tasks, knowledge, skills, abilities, work activities, work context, and professional role mapping
source_roles.codecademy: hands-on programming curriculum, concepts, projects, languages, data, AI, cybersecurity, and career-oriented learning paths

score_model.rule: Scores are evidence-backed and domain-specific; an overall score is never treated as universal intelligence.

mastery_gates: Complete realistic repository workflows when applicable
Demonstrate O*NET-aligned task performance for the selected occupation

beneficial_examples.task: Build and maintain a small inventory application
beneficial_examples.professional_output: working application, tests, documentation, reproducible build, benchmark report
validated analysis, charts, assumptions, source provenance, reproducible workflow, executive summary

beneficial_examples.task: Debug a failing production-style software workflow
beneficial_examples.professional_output: root cause, minimal reproduction, safe fix, regression test, evidence of passing result

mastery_rule: Completion of a course, repository exercise, or occupation description is not mastery by itself. Buddy must demonstrate transferable performance on independently generated tasks.
data_provenance: Store source identifiers and derived benchmark metadata. Do not copy proprietary course text or protected website content into benchmark datasets; create original task descriptions, tests, rubrics, and observations.
north_star: Turn learning resources into original, measurable, reusable benchmarks that make Buddy better at real work rather than merely better at passing lessons.
